text.title: Go Project Structure Decision Tree
text.summary: Routing tree mapping observable signals to a rule from content/01-core-rules.xml for go-project-structure. The first two branches route non-applicable inputs out; the remaining branches are blocking gates walked in order.

decision-tree.root-question: Is this a Go module that ships at least one binary and warrants the layout?

conclusion.verdict: SKIP — flat layout is fine at this scale
APPLY — cmd/ + internal/, pkg/ only for a named external importer
BLOCK — move handlers and queries into internal/
BLOCK — move it to internal/ before anyone outside can import it
BLOCK — invert one side via an interface declared at the consumer
BLOCK — move into cmd/ or internal/, or delete
BLOCK — add a Make target instead of another loose script
BLOCK — select on ctx.Done or a quit channel in every long-running goroutine
APPROVE — layout ready; run the vertical slice and the validator
SKIP — preconditions in Applies-If not met

text.example: Module + 2 binaries + 11 internal packages → neither skip branch matches → main is thin → nothing internal-only sits in pkg/ → no cycles → clean top level → every workflow has a Make target → workers select on ctx.Done → APPROVE.
